hooks.text: A new asteroid held a terrifying 3.1 percent chance of hitting Earth.
An asteroid with a 3.1 percent impact chance became the most threatening ever measured.
Could a newly discovered space rock really carry a 3.1 percent impact chance?

title: The Asteroid That Sparked a 3.1 Percent Impact Scare
description: How asteroid 2024 YR4 became the most threatening space rock ever measured before refined data cleared the threat.

beats.text: A new asteroid held a terrifying 3.1 percent chance of hitting Earth.
beats.visual: artist's concept of a stony near-Earth asteroid, 2024

beats.text: On December 27, 2024, the ATLAS telescope in Chile spotted asteroid 2024 YR4 sneaking past a solar blind spot.
queries: Asteroid Terrestrial-impact Last Alert System Chile

beats.text: This city-killer reached Level 3 on the Torino Scale, the highest impact hazard ever measured for its size.
beats.visual: The Torino Impact Hazard Scale chart, 2024

beats.text: Roughly 53 to 67 meters wide, it packed the explosive punch of 8 megatons of TNT.
beats.visual: Meteor Crater in Arizona aerial view, 2020

beats.text: A potential impact corridor stretched across Nigeria and South America, threatening millions for several weeks.
beats.visual: map of a global asteroid risk corridor, 2024

beats.text: Many feared a December 22, 2032 collision with an energy equivalent to 500 Hiroshima bombs.
subjects: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki

beats.text: Refined ground-based observatory and radar data cleared Earth, shifted the danger briefly to the Moon, and finally cleared both.
beats.visual: ground-based radio telescope dish tracking in desert, 2023

beats.text: Now, astronomers only remember the panic when a new asteroid held a terrifying 3.1 percent chance of hitting Earth.
beats.visual: artist's concept of an asteroid impact flash on the Moon, 2025

better_than_last: This version uses ground-based observatory imagery in beat 7, removes unnecessary phrasing to reduce runtime under 58 seconds, and maintains a flawless loop.
